intro: Today’s picks showcase new AI infrastructure, safety tools, and creative demos for builders, businesses, and investors.

picks.name: antirion
picks.what: The fastest open-source AI gateway – a single Rust binary with a console to route, secure, budget, and observe every LLM call across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and more.
picks.why: It lets developers manage LLM usage and guardrails centrally, useful for building production AI services.
picks.signal: 233 stars since 17 Oct, written in Rust

picks.name: Lampline
picks.what: Build AI phone agents on your own computer and test every change with an AI caller, open source, runs free with no API keys or cheap with your own keys.
picks.why: Provides a sandbox for developing and iterating conversational agents without external services.
picks.signal: 171 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python

picks.name: Basedash CSV Scheduler
picks.what: Ask once. Get a fresh CSV in Slack or email every week.
picks.why: Automates recurring data exports, saving time for teams that need regular reports.

picks.name: Wan2.2 14B Preview
picks.what: Generate a video from an image with a text prompt.
picks.why: Shows a high‑capacity model capable of text‑to‑video generation, a novel demo for creators.

picks.name: Argus
picks.what: Open source security platform to protect against agentic attacks.
picks.why: Offers tools to detect and mitigate malicious behavior in AI agents, relevant for safety‑focused developers.

picks.name: Corgi
picks.what: A helpful agent terminal multiplexer that shows what agents are doing, with shortcuts to navigate.
picks.why: Improves ergonomics for managing multiple AI agents in a single workflow.

picks.name: MemT-1.0
picks.what: Official repository for MemT-1.0, focusing on long‑context, long‑term memory for LLMs.
picks.why: Enables experiments with extended memory windows, useful for building agents that need persistent context.
picks.signal: 390 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python
